In spite of some pretty dated referential humour, there's still some valid reason to play this because they just don't make games like this anymore. I simply can't play these games legitimately because the puzzle solutions, like they are in pretty much every game of this style, take zero logical reasoning and just devolve into clicking around on the screen and combining objects until something happens. Play it with a guide and save yourself many, many hours.

There is no settings or menu button, no tutorial, nothing but old point and click adventure jank that works with the humor of this game.

Like a lot of LucasArts classics, I've constantly returned to this over the years. While a little obtuse, like most of them, Sam & Max is just the pinnacle for me. The gorgeous animation is still stunning, and, well, it just cracks me up, little buddy.

Sam & Max Hit the Road is peak 90s LucasArts: sharp writing, unhinged humor, and two freelance police officers who solve crimes with the grace of a car crash. Built on the SCUMM engine and one of LucasArts’ first fully voice‑acted adventures, it still feels alive thanks to the iMUSE music system and Bill Farmer’s iconic performance as Sam.

Highlights:
- Comedy that hits harder than it has any right to.
- Voice acting that defined the duo for decades.
- A cross‑country tour of America’s weirdest attractions.
- Puzzles that bounce between clever and cartoon‑logic chaos.

Cons:
- A couple puzzles and minigames show their age.
- The humor is aggressively 90s — which you’ll either love or fear.

10/10.  
A hilarious, stylish, technically impressive classic that still earns its cult status.

You will hit the road. You will not like it at first, believe me. You will realize that you suck at point-n'-click games. You will form a maternal affection for Max. You will look up a guide, use it for one puzzle, and then close it, believing that you won't need it again. In two minutes, you will be opening your browser again for that exact same guide. You will begin to watch your pride drift away, and every achievement you have ever gotten in a video game will turn out to have meant nothing to this test of strength. You will, at first, not understand the functions of each of the function tools. You will use Look on everything. You will not know how to save your game, and, once you have made considerable progress, you will close the window and it'll alllll go away. All of it. You will proclaim in your agony, "Oh, why didn't I buy this game while it was on sale?" You will consider refunding it. But then you will realize that, of course, you spent too long playing it. And ya bought it two months ago.

Got this on sale due to childhood nostalgia since i started this over and over on my dads PC when I was young and internet wasn't even a thing yet. Finally finished it and some of the humor and character interactions still hold up well. The overall story and especially the ending don't make much sense though. Some of the clues, items and combinations require a guide as well, or a lot of trial and error if you wan't to progress in the game, which i guess is the lost art of old point & click adventures if you wanna call it that. 

In the end, the story and ending left a lot to be desired and most of the in-game destinations are just a setup for gags, so i wouldn't recommend playing this nowadays, if you don't have any nostalgia for it. If you do enjoy point & click adventures though, it's one of the good ones i'd say!

It's awesome revisiting the classics. Could have easily found a free version, but $2 to play it on the deck with no fuss? Heck yeah.

Es una pequeña gran aventura, humor marca de la casa, quizá un poquito más bestia de lo que acostumbra LucasArt, aunque dentro siempre de lo disfrutable, por supuestísimo. La idea es muy buena, la trama y diálogos están llenos de referencias a otros juegos de lucasart y la cultura pop, y los puzzles no son demasiado locos, salvo un par de puntos. La verdad es que merece mucho la pena jugarlo, es cortito, agradable, unas 6 horas sin guías. (bueno, para ser honestos me lo pasé en los 90 y aún recordaba la solución de los dos puzzles que se me atragantaron durante semanas en su día.)

Me gusta bastante que la dificultad de los puzzles sea gradual, porque, en comparación con Grim Fandango, el 80% del juego de la calavera me lo pase con guia, mientras que aqui, como 2 veces contadas tuve que usar guia. Tal vez no le suene a algunos, pero que buen juego mae.

Si pueden, jueguenlo, el final es demasiado safisfactorio, y los personajes ridisurdos, la musica excelente.

Ademas, EL JUEGO TRAE UN PAINT Y UN BATTLESHIP INCLUIDOS!!
